# Proposed cases for ENG-2228

## Acceptance (Done When)

- [ ] **A selected text shape offers Edit link, like a geo shape** `dw1-a-selected-text-shape-offers-edit-link-l` — proposed
  - Do: Select the geo shape and open its context menu; note the Edit link item. Then select only the text shape and open its context menu. Also try the Edit link keyboard shortcut with the text shape selected.
  - Passes if: The text shape's context menu shows Edit link in the same place as for the geo shape, and choosing it or the shortcut opens the Edit link dialog with an empty https:// field.
  - priority: P1
  - protects: Text shapes expose the link action through the same menu and shortcut as geo shapes.
  - fails when: The menu-hooks patch is not applied or the eligibility gate excludes text shapes, so Edit link is missing for text.
  - why new: No kit exists yet; nothing covers the Edit link action on any shape.
  - given: A canvas containing one text shape and one geo (rectangle) shape, neither linked.
  - variant: Locked text shape: Edit link is not offered, matching a locked geo shape
  - variant: Two shapes selected: Edit link is not offered
- [ ] **Adding a page link to a text shape shows a link button that opens the note** `dw2-adding-a-page-link-to-a-text-shape-shows` — proposed
  - Do: Select the text shape, choose Edit link, paste the Obsidian link to Source.md (Copy Obsidian URL), and save. Click the link button that appears next to the text.
  - Passes if: A link button appears beside the text shape, styled like a geo shape's link button, with the URL as its tooltip. Clicking it opens Source.md in the sidebar and deselects the shape; no OS 'open with' prompt appears.
  - priority: P1
  - protects: Adding a link to a text shape and following it to the linked note.
  - fails when: The meta.url is not written, the overlay does not render the button, or navigation is not intercepted so the obsidian:// URI goes to the OS handler.
  - why new: No kit exists yet.
  - given: A canvas with an unlinked text shape, and a note named Source.md in the vault.
  - variant: Cmd/Ctrl-click opens the note in a new tab
  - variant: Alt-click opens the note in a new leaf
  - variant: An https:// URL link opens in the external browser
  - variant: A bare domain like example.com is saved as https://example.com
- [ ] **Editing a text shape's link changes where its link button goes** `dw2-editing-a-text-shape-s-link-changes-wher` — proposed
  - Do: Select the text shape, choose Edit link, replace the URL with Other.md's Obsidian link, and save. Click the link button.
  - Passes if: The dialog opened prefilled with the Source.md link; after saving, the button tooltip shows the Other.md link and clicking it opens Other.md.
  - priority: P1
  - protects: Changing an existing text-shape link.
  - fails when: readLinkUrl does not prefill from meta, or the update writes to props instead of meta for text shapes.
  - why new: No kit exists yet.
  - given: A canvas with a text shape already linked to Source.md, and a second note Other.md in the vault.
  - variant: Cancel after changing the URL leaves the original link
  - variant: Typing an invalid URL disables Save and Enter does nothing
  - variant: Undo after saving restores the previous link
- [ ] **Removing a text shape's link hides its link button** `dw2-removing-a-text-shape-s-link-hides-its-l` — proposed
  - Do: Select the text shape, choose Edit link, and use the remove/clear link button in the dialog.
  - Passes if: The link button beside the text disappears, the text itself is unchanged, and reopening Edit link shows an empty https:// field.
  - priority: P1
  - protects: Removing a link from a text shape.
  - fails when: handleClear patches props.url on a text shape (validation error) or leaves meta.url set, so the button stays.
  - why new: No kit exists yet.
  - given: A canvas with a text shape linked to Source.md.
  - variant: Clearing the field so it is invalid switches the dialog to its remove state, like a geo shape
- [ ] **A text shape's link survives closing and reopening the canvas** `dw3-a-text-shape-s-link-survives-closing-and` — proposed
  - Do: Close the canvas tab, reopen the canvas file, and click the text shape's link button. Then reload Obsidian and check again.
  - Passes if: After reopen and after reload, the link button is still beside the text shape and opens Source.md; the canvas file's stored text shape record holds the link URL.
  - priority: P0
  - protects: Text-shape links are saved to the canvas file and not silently dropped.
  - fails when: meta changes are not autosaved or meta.url is stripped on load, losing the user's link.
  - why new: No kit exists yet.
  - given: A canvas with a text shape linked to Source.md, saved.
  - variant: A link removed before closing stays removed after reopen

## Regression: Edit link dialog on geo, note and bookmark shapes

_Why: The actions override in TldrawViewComponent replaces the stock edit-link onSelect for every shape type with the forked TextLinkDialog, so adding, editing, clearing and validating links on existing geo/note/bookmark shapes now runs through new validateUrl/linkPatch code instead of tldraw's EditLinkDialog. (risk 3×2=6). Files: apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/TldrawViewComponent.tsx, apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/TextLinkDialog.tsx_

- [ ] **Geo, note and bookmark shapes still add, edit and remove links through Edit link** `qa-geo-note-and-bookmark-shapes-still-add-e` — proposed
  - Do: For the rectangle and the note: choose Edit link, enter https://example.com, save; reopen Edit link and change it; then remove it. For the bookmark: open Edit link and try an Obsidian page link.
  - Passes if: Rectangle and note show tldraw's link button after saving, the dialog prefills the saved URL when reopened, and the button disappears after removal. The bookmark dialog rejects the obsidian:// link (Save disabled) but accepts an https URL.
  - priority: P1
  - protects: Link editing on shape types that already supported it before this PR.
  - fails when: The forked TextLinkDialog writes meta instead of props for geo, mis-validates input, or the override breaks the stock dialog for non-text shapes.
  - why new: No kit exists yet; the acceptance cases only exercise text shapes.
  - given: A canvas with an unlinked rectangle, an unlinked note shape, and a bookmark shape.
  - variant: Rectangle with an Obsidian page link saves and shows a link button
  - variant: Pasting a full URL after the prefilled https:// keeps a single protocol
  - variant: Undo after saving a geo link restores the previous value
  - variant: Edit link is unavailable while a non-select tool is active

## Regression: Opening a link from a geo shape's link button

_Why: The tldraw patch rewrites HyperlinkButton to dispatch a cancelable tldraw.navigate-link event and drop href for non-web URLs, and registerLinkNavigation intercepts obsidian:// links, so clicking an existing https link on a geo shape could stop opening in the browser or get swallowed. (risk 3×2=6). Files: patches/tldraw@3.14.2.patch, apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/linkNavigation.ts, apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/TldrawViewComponent.tsx_

- [ ] **A geo shape's web link still opens in the browser and page links open in the vault** `qa-a-geo-shape-s-web-link-still-opens-in-th` — proposed
  - Do: Click the link button on the https rectangle. Then click the link button on the Obsidian-linked rectangle.
  - Passes if: The https link opens in the external browser and the canvas stays put. The Obsidian link opens Source.md in the sidebar without an OS prompt.
  - priority: P1
  - protects: Following existing links from geo shapes.
  - fails when: The patched HyperlinkButton prevents default on web URLs, drops href, or the listener catches non-obsidian links.
  - why new: No kit exists yet; the text-shape acceptance case covers only text overlay buttons.
  - given: A canvas with one rectangle linked to https://example.com and one linked to the Obsidian URL of Source.md.
  - variant: Obsidian link to a file that does not exist shows a 'Cannot open link' warning and opens nothing
  - variant: Obsidian link pointing to another vault shows the same warning
  - variant: mailto: link still hands off to the mail client

## Regression: Opening an existing canvas that contains linked shapes

_Why: The @tldraw/validate patch changes T.linkUrl, which validates every shape's url prop when a canvas file is loaded, so a canvas saved before this PR with geo links could fail validation and not open. (risk 2×3=6). Files: patches/@tldraw__validate@3.14.2.patch, pnpm-workspace.yaml_

- [ ] **A canvas saved before this change with linked shapes still opens** `qa-a-canvas-saved-before-this-change-with-l` — proposed
  - Do: Open the fixture canvas.
  - Passes if: The canvas opens with all shapes present, the linked rectangle shows its link button, and no validation error notice appears.
  - priority: P1
  - protects: Existing canvases keep loading after the validator patch.
  - fails when: The patched linkUrl validator rejects a previously valid stored URL, so the canvas fails to load.
  - why new: No kit exists yet; no case loads a pre-existing canvas file.
  - given: A fixture canvas file created on main containing a rectangle linked to https://example.com, a rectangle with an empty link, and a bookmark shape.
  - variant: Fixture rectangle whose stored URL uses uppercase 'Obsidian://open?file=' still loads and opens the note

## Questions before steps are written

- **Adding a page link to a text shape shows a link button that opens the note**: The text-shape button sits outside the right edge, vertically centred, while geo shapes show it inside the shape corner. Is that the accepted 'same visual affordance', or should the position match geo?
- **geo-link-button-open**: How should the runner confirm that an https link opened in the external browser from the Obsidian app: is observing that no in-vault navigation happened and the click was not prevented enough?
- **A selected text shape offers Edit link, like a geo shape**: Which keyboard shortcut should the case use for Edit link in this Obsidian build (tldraw default Cmd/Ctrl+K), or should only the context menu be checked?

## Not checked end to end

- Done When 4: Unit test coverage of link persistence and text-shape eligibility is checked in the test suite, not through the UI.

## Assumptions (not tied to a changed line)

- TextLinkOverlay only shows a button when the whole text shape is inside the viewport (viewport.includes(bounds)), and does not follow rotation or frame clipping; this looks deliberate per the code comment, so no case tests partially off-screen or rotated text.
- Duplicating or copy-pasting a linked text shape likely carries meta.url to the copy; not proposed as a case because the diff does not change duplication code.
- The diff text was truncated in the prompt (part of TextLinkDialog JSX and the ESM tldraw patch); cases assume the ESM patch mirrors the CJS patch shown.

content.text:
`propose.ts` is drafted and I ran it on ENG-2228; the review file it produced is attached. Its 65 unit tests pass and it type-checks. Nothing is committed yet: the runner and `propose` are both uncommitted in `~/Desktop/code/proof-kit`, branch `obsidian-runner`.

**How it works.** It lives in `prototypes/proof-runner/propose/` and has three steps:
1. **`prompt`** gathers the ticket's Done When, the PR diff (`--base`/`--head`, so a merged branch works too) and the existing kit, including rejected cases and their reasons. It fills these into `PROMPT.md`, which it reads at runtime so the prompt can change without a rebuild. No API key is needed: the agent in your session answers the prompt.
2. **`merge`** checks the answer, keeps what passes as `proposed` cases (`by: "model"`), and writes `<kit>.review.md` plus a side file with questions and assumptions. What it checks:
   - every surface area's files appear in the diff
   - every acceptance case's Done When number exists on the ticket
   - regression cases are kept only where risk (probability × impact) is 3 or more
   - no near-duplicate of an existing case, including rejected ones
   - every Done When bullet has a case or a stated reason it isn't end-to-end testable
3. **`decide --by <person>`** records approvals, and rejections with a reason. It refuses names like Claude, model or agent, which closes the "Claude, for sid" gap.

**What the prompt borrows from the research:**
- BMAD: grounding rules, the probability × impact scale, P0–P3 priority
- gstack: the four-question value card, mapping changed files to features, questions it can't answer
- Playwright's planner: cases independent, fresh starting state
- Autonoma: each case argues why existing cases don't cover it
- Qodo: never re-propose rejected cases

**ENG-2228 result, from an agent that saw only the prompt:** 5 surface areas, 8 cases and 3 questions; none were dropped.

| | Blind proposal | My hand-written kit |
|---|---|---|

content.text:
Possible, but one caveat to settle first. The trace viewer is **step-through replay**, not re-execution. A reviewer can click each action and see the DOM snapshot before and after it, the screenshot, console output and timing, but can't re-run a step from inside the viewer. Re-running step by step is already what our runner's caption bar does live (step mode, Retry). So the combination would be: **trace viewer for async review, plus "rerun this case in step mode" when a reviewer wants to poke at it.**

Technically there's one condition: actions only appear in a trace if **Playwright** performs them. Our executor sends raw CDP. So the change is to drive Obsidian through Playwright's `connectOverCDP` while keeping our checks, and wrap each kit case and step in a named `tracing.group(...)`. Whether Playwright tracing works over CDP on Electron is the unverified part, so I'm spiking that first. Checking what's available:

The runner now records a Playwright trace you can step through in the trace viewer. The full ENG-2228 kit passed 8/8 with tracing on, and the attached screenshots show it in the viewer.

**What a reviewer gets:**
- **An outline:** Setup, then `Case 2/8: Add a page link to a text shape`, then `Step 9: save the link`, then the click itself. Each case ends with a `Check: …` group for the pass condition.
- **Per action:** a styled snapshot of Obsidian before and after, with a red dot where it clicked. Also the parameters (coordinates, the exact text typed, the key pressed, the kit's js), plus console, network and timing.
- **A filmstrip** across the top to scrub through the whole run. Sid's caption bar shows in each frame, so you can see which case and step was running.

**How a reviewer opens it:** run `npx playwright show-trace trace.zip`, or drag the file onto trace.playwright.dev. That page works entirely in the browser; nothing is uploaded.

**One limit:** the viewer replays and lets you inspect each step, but it can't re-run one. Re-running is our runner's job: run the case again in step mode from the caption bar, or edit the step and run again.

**How it works:** add `--trace` to the runner.
- Visible actions go through Playwright attached to Obsidian, so each becomes a trace step: clicks, keys, typing, js steps and checks.
- The 100 ms readiness polling and caption-bar updates stay on raw CDP, so they don't clutter the trace.
- Each kit case and step becomes a trace group, opened just before it acts. The Machine's own render calls run behind it and put actions in the wrong step.
- Obsidian loads its CSS from `app://`, which trace snapshots can't capture. The runner copies those rules inline while tracing, then puts them back.

**Problems found while building it:**
- **Size:** the trace is 76 MB, mostly ~3k screenshot frames. That's fine locally, but too big to attach to every PR. Options: drop the filmstrip and keep the snapshots, or host it on the `/releases` Vercel Blob as discussed. The scrubbing caveat from before still applies there.
- **The built-in browser pane can't open the viewer.** The viewer needs a service worker, and the pane shows a blank page. A normal Chrome, or headless Chromium as I used, works fine.
- **Waits don't appear as actions.** "Wait for the link dialog" shows up as an empty step. Turning `wait_for` into a Playwright `waitForSelector` would make it visible.

**State of things:**
- `playwright-core` was added to the proof-runner package.
- 65/65 tests pass and everything type-checks.
- `testVault2` is now leased to my eng-2369 worktree.
- Still nothing committed on `obsidian-runner`: the runner, `propose`, and now tracing.

Can I commit locally now?

Learn how Astr Full cross-link map for this page: [/docs/vercel-blob.graph.md](/docs/vercel-blob.graph.md) ## Use cases You can upload files to Vercel Blob at build time or at runtime (for example, when users submit files). Common use cases include: - Files for display and download such as avatars, screenshots, cover images, and videos - Large files such as video and audio to take advantage of the global network - Persistent preferences and context for [eve agents](#store-eve-agent-memory) - Files that you would normally store in an external file storage solution like Amazon S3. With your project hosted on Vercel, you can readily access and manage these files with Vercel Blob > **💡 Note:** Stored files are referred to as "blobs" once they're in the storage system, > following cloud storage terminology. ## Private and public storage Files are private or public depending on the store you create. The access mode defines how files are accessed and delivered. Use the following table to understand the differences between the two modes: | | Private storage | Public storage | | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | | Write access | Authenticated | Authenticated | | Read access | Authenticated (token required) | Anyone with the URL | | Delivery | Through your [Functions](/docs/functions), which fetch the blob with the SDK | Direct blob URL | | Best for | Sensitive documents, user content, custom auth | Large media, images, videos, public assets | > **💡 Note:** It's important to choose the correct access mode for your use case since you cannot change it after the creation of a blob store. Learn more about [private storage](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage) and [public storage](/docs/vercel-blob/public-storage). ## Getting started Upload a file with the Vercel Blob SDK: **index.ts** ```ts filename="index.ts" import { put } from '@vercel/blob'; const blob = await put('avatar.jpg', imageFile, { access: 'private' /* or 'public' */, }); ``` **main.py** ```py filename="main.py" from vercel import blob uploaded = await blob.put_blob( "avatar.jpg", image_bytes, access="private", # or "public" ) ``` You can create and manage your Vercel Blob stores from your [account dashboard](/dashboard) or the [Vercel CLI](/docs/cli/blob). You can create blob stores in any of the 19 [regions](/docs/regions#region-list) to optimize performance and meet data residency requirements. You can scope your Vercel Blob stores to your Hobby team or [team](/docs/accounts#creating-a-team), and [connect them to as many projects as you want](#connecting-a-store-to-your-projects). To get started, see the [server-side](/docs/vercel-blob/server-upload), or [client-side](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload) quickstart guides. Or visit the full API reference for the [JS SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk) or the [Python SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/python-sdk-reference). ## Store eve agent memory Use [eve](/docs/eve)'s built-in `fileMemory()` provider to persist short user preferences and stable facts across conversations in a [private Vercel Blob store](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage). Each memory scope has its own document, which eve recalls before each turn. The model updates memory with `save_memory` and `remove_memory` tools. To add file memory to an existing eve project, run: ```bash filename="terminal" eve add memory/file ``` Choose **Install and set up** to create the memory definition in `agent/memory/file.ts` and create or reuse a private Blob store connected to your linked project through OIDC. When you run `eve dev` locally, memory stays in the development process and clears when you restart it. For a working example, deploy the [eve Memory Agent template](/templates/eve/eve-memory-agent). The Slack assistant keeps personal preferences separate from shared channel conventions, using authenticated user and channel identities to determine who shares each memory. See the [template repository](https://github.com/vercel-labs/eve-memory-agent-template) for setup and customization. Read [Choose an eve memory provider](/kb/guide/choose-an-eve-memory-provider) for file memory configuration and a comparison with providers that support semantic retrieval or automatic capture. ## Connecting a store to your projects To read and write blobs from your code, connect the store to your project: 1. Go to your Blob store's **Projects** tab 2. Select **Connect to Project** 3. Choose the project and the environments to connect One store can serve multiple projects, and one project can use multiple stores. ### OIDC access by default Connected projects authenticate with OpenID Connect (OIDC) by default. When you connect a store, Vercel adds these environment variables to your project: | Environment variable | What it is | | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `BLOB_STORE_ID` | The id of your Blob store. The SDK pairs it with the OIDC token to authenticate requests. It's an identifier, not a secret. | | `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` | A short-lived OIDC token that Vercel issues and rotates automatically. You never handle it directly. | | `BLOB_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_KEY` | The public key the SDK uses to verify webhook callbacks signed by Vercel Blob. It's a public value, not a secret. | The SDK reads these variables automatically, and you never need to read or pass the OIDC token yourself. Code running in [Vercel Functions](/docs/functions) and builds works out of the box. Local development works after you run `vercel env pull` once: when the token expires, the SDK refreshes it automatically using your Vercel CLI credentials. Because OIDC tokens rotate automatically, no long-lived secret can leak from your codebase or environment. Learn more about [how OIDC token federation works](/docs/oidc#how-oidc-token-federation-works). ### When to use a read-write token `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` is a long-lived static token added to your project when you create a store. OIDC takes precedence when its environment variables are present. Use the read-write token only when: - Your code runs outside Vercel, such as in a CI job or on another host - You generate client tokens for [browser uploads](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload) See Authentication in the [JS SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk#authentication) or [Python SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/python-sdk-reference#authentication) reference for the full credential resolution order. ## Using Vercel Blob in your workflow If you'd like to know whether or not Vercel Blob can be integrated into your workflow, it's worth knowing the following: - You can have one or more Vercel Blob stores per Vercel account - You can use multiple Vercel Blob stores in one Vercel project - Each Vercel Blob store can be accessed by multiple Vercel projects - Read access: - With private Blob stores: all read access requires authentication - With public Blob stores: blob URLs are accessible to anyone with the link - Write access: all writes require authentication, through [OIDC](#oidc-access-by-default) by default on Vercel, or a [read-write token](#when-to-use-a-read-write-token) elsewhere ### Transferring to another project If you need to transfer your blob store from one project to another project in the same or different team, review [Transferring your store](/docs/storage#transferring-your-store). ## Caching Vercel's [CDN cache](/docs/caching/cdn-cache) caches all blobs (private and public) for up to 1 month by default. You can customize this duration by setting a cache max age when you upload a blob. The difference is in how the cache is reached: - **Public blobs**: The browser hits the CDN cache directly. Both the CDN and browser cache the blob. See [public storage caching](/docs/vercel-blob/public-storage#caching) for full details. - **Private blobs**: Your [Function](/docs/functions) fetches the blob through the CDN, then streams the response to the browser. You separately control browser caching through the `Cache-Control` header on your Function's response. See [private storage caching](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage#caching) for recommendations. ### Important considerations when updating blobs When you delete or update (overwrite) a blob, the changes may take up to 60 seconds to propagate through our cache. However, browser caching presents additional challenges: - While our cache can update to serve the latest content, browsers will continue serving the cached version - To force browsers to fetch the updated content, add a unique query parameter to the blob URL: ```html ``` For private blobs served through your [Functions](/docs/functions), your server code can skip the propagation delay entirely and read the latest version with a [consistent read](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage#consistent-reads). For more information about updating existing blobs, see the [overwriting blobs](#overwriting-blobs) section. ### Best practice: Treat blobs as immutable For optimal performance and to avoid caching issues, consider treating blobs as immutable objects: - Instead of updating existing blobs, create new ones with different pathnames, or add a [random suffix](#alternatives-to-overwriting) when you upload - This approach avoids unexpected behaviors like outdated content appearing in your application There are still valid use cases for mutable blobs with shorter cache durations, such as a single JSON file that's updated every 5 minutes with a top list of sales or other regularly refreshed data. For these scenarios, set an appropriate cache max age when you upload and be mindful of caching behaviors. ## Overwriting blobs By default, Vercel Blob prevents you from accidentally overwriting existing blobs by using the same pathname twice. When you attempt to upload a blob with a pathname that already exists, the upload fails with an error. ### Allowing overwrites To explicitly allow overwriting an existing blob, enable overwriting when you upload: **index.ts** ```ts filename="index.ts" const blob = await put('user-profile.jpg', imageFile, { access: 'private' /* or 'public' */, allowOverwrite: true, // Enable overwriting an existing blob with the same pathname }); ``` **main.py** ```py filename="main.py" uploaded = await blob.put_blob( "user-profile.jpg", image_bytes, access="private", # or "public" allow_overwrite=True, # Enable overwriting an existing blob with the same pathname ) ``` You can allow overwrites for server uploads, and for [client uploads](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload) when your server generates the client token. ### When to use overwriting Overwriting blobs can be appropriate for certain use cases: 1. **Regularly updated files**: For files that need to maintain the same URL but contain updated content (like JSON data files or configuration files) 2. **Content with predictable update patterns**: For data that changes on a schedule and where consumers expect updates at the same URL When overwriting blobs, be aware that due to [caching](#caching), changes won't be immediately visible. Changes may take up to 60 seconds to propagate, and browser caches may need to be explicitly refreshed. For private blobs, you can read the latest version immediately with a [consistent read](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage#consistent-reads). ### Alternatives to overwriting If you want to avoid overwriting existing content (recommended for most use cases), you have two options: 1. **Add a random suffix**: The SDK adds a unique random suffix to your pathname: **index.ts** ```ts filename="index.ts" const blob = await put('avatar.jpg', imageFile, { access: 'private' /* or 'public' */, addRandomSuffix: true, // Creates a pathname like 'REDACTED.jpg' }); ``` **main.py** ```py filename="main.py" uploaded = await blob.put_blob( "avatar.jpg", image_bytes, access="private", # or "public" add_random_suffix=True, # Creates a pathname like 'REDACTED.jpg' ) ``` 2. **Generate unique pathnames programmatically**: Create unique pathnames by adding timestamps, UUIDs, or other identifiers: **index.ts** ```ts filename="index.ts" const timestamp = Date.now(); const blob = await put(`user-profile-${timestamp}.jpg`, imageFile, { access: 'private' /* or 'public' */, }); ``` **main.py** ```py filename="main.py" import time timestamp = time.time_ns() // 1_000_000 uploaded = await blob.put_blob( f"user-profile-{timestamp}.jpg", image_bytes, access="private", # or "public" ) ``` ## Conditional writes Conditional writes implement optimistic concurrency control. When writing, pass a known ETag from a previous upload, download, or metadata request. The operation only succeeds if the blob hasn't changed since that ETag was issued. If another process modified the blob in between, the ETag won't match and the SDK raises a precondition failed error. This works the same way for both private and public storage, and applies to uploads, copies, and deletes. See the [JS SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk#put) and [Python SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/python-sdk-reference#copy_blob) references for the conditional operations each SDK supports: ```js import { head, put, BlobPreconditionFailedError } from '@vercel/blob'; // 1. Read the current blob and its ETag const metadata = await head('config.json'); // 2. Write with the ETag — only succeeds if the blob hasn't changed try { await put('config.json', JSON.stringify(newConfig), { access: 'private' /* or 'public' */, allowOverwrite: true, ifMatch: metadata.etag, }); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof BlobPreconditionFailedError) { // The blob was modified by another process — retry or handle the conflict } throw error; } ``` Use conditional writes when multiple processes or users may update the same blob concurrently, such as shared configuration files or collaborative documents. ## Conditional reads Conditional reads avoid re-downloading blobs that haven't changed. Pass the ETag you received from a previous response, and if the blob is unchanged, the read returns a `304 Not Modified` status without the file content. Pass the ETag with the [`ifNoneMatch`](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk#get) option. How conditional reads work depends on how blobs are delivered: - **Private blobs**: Your [Function](/docs/functions) fetches the blob with a conditional read, then forwards the `304` or `200` response to the browser. See [browser caching with conditional requests](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage#browser-caching-with-conditional-requests) for a full example. - **Public blobs**: The CDN handles conditional requests automatically. When a browser requests a public blob URL, the CDN includes an ETag in the response. On repeat requests, the browser sends `If-None-Match` and the CDN returns `304 Not Modified` when the blob hasn't changed. See [browser caching](/docs/vercel-blob/public-storage#browser-caching-with-conditional-requests) for details. ## Blob Data Transfer Understanding Blob Data Transfer helps you manage your [usage and pricing](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing). Blob Data Transfer applies to **public blob** downloads and to your [Functions](/docs/functions) fetching private blobs from the store. When delivering private blobs to end users, [Fast Data Transfer](/docs/cdn) applies on the Function response. See [delivery costs](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing#private-and-public-storage-delivery-costs). Vercel Blob delivers content through a specialized network optimized for static assets: - **Region-based distribution**: Content is served from 19 regional hubs strategically located around the world - **Optimized for non-critical assets**: Well-suited for content "below the fold" that isn't essential for initial page rendering metrics like First Contentful Paint (FCP) or Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) - **Cost-optimized for large assets**: 3x more cost-efficient than [Fast Data Transfer](/docs/cdn) on average - **Great for media delivery**: Ideal for large media files like images, videos, and documents While [Fast Data Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-data-transfer) provides city-level, ultra-low latency, Blob Data Transfer prioritizes cost-efficiency for larger assets where ultra-low latency isn't essential. Blob Data Transfer fees apply only to downloads (outbound traffic), not uploads. See download charges for [private storage](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage#download-charges) and [public storage](/docs/vercel-blob/public-storage#download-charges), or the [pricing documentation](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing) for full details. ## Upload charges Client uploads have no data transfer charges. Server uploads incur [Fast Data Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-data-transfer) charges when your Vercel application receives the file. See download and upload charge details on the [private storage](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage#upload-charges) and [public storage](/docs/vercel-blob/public-storage#upload-charges) pages. ## Choosing your Blob store region You can create Blob stores in any of the 19 [regions](/docs/regions#region-list). Use the region selector in the dashboard at blob store creation time, or use the [CLI](/docs/cli/blob) with the `--region` option. Select a region close to your customers and functions to minimize upload time. Region selection also helps meet data regulatory requirements. Vercel Blob [pricing](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing) is regionalized, so check the pricing for your selected region. You cannot change the region once the store is created. ## Simple operations Simple operations in Vercel Blob are specific read actions counted for billing purposes: - When you retrieve blob metadata without downloading the blob - When a blob is accessed by its URL and it's a cache MISS A cache MISS occurs when the blob is accessed for the first time or when its previously cached version has expired. Note that blob URL access resulting in a cache HIT does not count as a Simple Operation. ## Advanced operations Advanced operations in Vercel Blob are write, copy, and listing actions counted for billing purposes: - When you upload a blob from your server - When you upload a blob from the browser with a [client upload](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload) - When you copy an existing blob - When you list blobs in your store ### Dashboard usage counts as operations Using the Vercel Blob file browser in your dashboard will count as operations. Each time you refresh the blob list, upload files through the dashboard, or view blob details, these actions use the same API methods that count toward your usage limits and billing. Common dashboard actions that count as operations: - **Refreshing the file browser**: Lists your blobs - **Uploading files via dashboard**: Uploads each file - **Viewing blob details**: May trigger additional API calls - **Navigating folders**: Lists blobs with different prefixes If you notice unexpected increases in your operations count, check whether team members are browsing your blob store through the Vercel dashboard. For [multipart uploads](#multipart-uploads), multiple advanced operations are counted: - One operation when starting the upload - One operation for each part uploaded - One operation for completing the upload Delete operations are free of charge. They are considered advanced operations for [operation rate limits](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing#operation-rate-limits) but not for billing. ## Storage calculation Vercel Blob measures your storage usage by taking snapshots of your blob store size every 15 minutes and averages these measurements over the entire month to calculate your GB-month usage. This approach accounts for fluctuations in storage as blobs are added and removed, ensuring you're only billed for your actual usage over time, not peak usage. The Vercel dashboard displays two metrics: - **Latest value**: The most recent measurement of your blob store size - **Monthly average**: The average of all measurements throughout the billing period (this is what you're billed for) **Example:** 1. Day 1: Upload a 2GB file → Store size: 2GB 2. Day 15: Add 1GB file → Store size: 3GB 3. Day 25: Delete 2GB file → Store size: 1GB Month end billing: - Latest value: 1GB - Monthly average: ~2GB (billed amount) If no changes occur in the following month (no new uploads or deletions), each 15-minute measurement would consistently show 1 GB. In this case, your next month's billing would be exactly 1 GB/month, as your monthly average would equal your latest value. ## Multipart uploads Vercel Blob supports multipart uploads for large files, which provides significant advantages when transferring substantial amounts of data. Multipart uploads work by splitting large files into smaller chunks (parts) that are uploaded independently and then reassembled on the server. This approach offers several key benefits: - **Improved upload reliability**: If a network issue occurs during upload, only the affected part needs to be retried instead of restarting the entire upload - **Better performance**: Multiple parts can be uploaded in parallel, significantly increasing transfer speed - **Progress tracking**: More granular upload progress reporting as each part completes We recommend using multipart uploads for files larger than 100 MB. See multipart uploads in the [JS SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk#multipart-uploads) and [Python SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/python-sdk-reference#upload-a-blob-in-parts) references for how each SDK splits and uploads parts. For billing purposes, multipart uploads count as multiple advanced operations: - One operation when starting the upload - One operation for each part uploaded - One operation for completing the upload This approach ensures reliable handling of large files while maintaining the performance and efficiency expected from modern cloud storage solutions. ## Durability and availability Vercel Blob leverages [Amazon S3](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/) as its underlying storage infrastructure, providing industry-leading durability and availability: - **Durability**: Vercel Blob offers 99.999999999% (11 nines) durability. This means that even with one billion objects, you could expect to go a hundred years without losing a single one. - **Availability**: Vercel Blob provides 99.99% (4 nines) availability in a given year, ensuring that your data is accessible when you need it. These guarantees are backed by [S3's robust architecture](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/DataDurability.html), which includes automatic replication and error correction mechanisms. ## Folders and slashes Vercel Blob has folders support to organize your blobs: **index.ts** ```ts filename="index.ts" const blob = await put('folder/file.txt', 'Hello World!', { access: 'private' /* or 'public' */, }); ``` **main.py** ```py filename="main.py" uploaded = await blob.put_blob( "folder/file.txt", b"Hello World!", access="private", # or "public" ) ``` The path `folder/file.txt` creates a folder named `folder` and a blob named `file.txt`. To list all blobs within a folder, list blobs with the folder as a prefix: **index.ts** ```ts filename="index.ts" const listOfBlobs = await list({ cursor, limit: 1000, prefix: 'folder/', }); ``` **main.py** ```py filename="main.py" async for item in blob.query_blobs(prefix="folder/"): print(item.pathname) ``` To browse one folder level at a time, list only the blobs directly inside the folder along with the names of its subfolders. See browsing folders in the [JS SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk#folders) and [Python SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/python-sdk-reference#query_blob_entries) references. You don't need to create folders. Upload a file with a path containing a slash `/`, and Vercel Blob will interpret the slashes as folder delimiters. In the Vercel Blob file browser on the Vercel dashboard, any pathname with a slash `/` is treated as a folder. However, these are not actual folders like in a traditional file system; they are used for organizing blobs in listings and the file browser. ## Pathname characters Control characters in a pathname are not supported. If you upload a blob with one, the pathname and URLs returned when you list blobs may not match the blob you stored, and operations that take them may not find it. ## Blob sorting and organization When you list blobs, they're returned in **lexicographical order** by pathname (not creation date). Numbers are treated as characters, so `file10.txt` comes before `file2.txt`. **Sort by creation date:** Include timestamps in pathnames: **index.ts** ```ts filename="index.ts" const timestamp = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]; // YYYY-MM-DD await put(`reports/${timestamp}-quarterly-report.pdf`, file, { access: 'private' /* or 'public' */, }); ``` **main.py** ```py filename="main.py" from datetime import date timestamp = date.today().isoformat() # YYYY-MM-DD await blob.put_blob( f"reports/{timestamp}-quarterly-report.pdf", file_bytes, access="private", # or "public" ) ``` **Use prefixes for search:** Consider lowercase pathnames for consistent matching: **index.ts** ```ts filename="index.ts" await put('user-uploads/avatar.jpg', file, { access: 'private' /* or 'public' */, }); const userUploads = await list({ prefix: 'user-uploads/' }); ``` **main.py** ```py filename="main.py" await blob.put_blob( "user-uploads/avatar.jpg", file_bytes, access="private", # or "public" ) user_uploads = [item async for item in blob.query_blobs(prefix="user-uploads/")] ``` For complex sorting, sort results client-side using the upload time or other properties. ## More resources - [Private Storage](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage) - [Public Storage](/docs/vercel-blob/public-storage) - [Client Upload Quickstart](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload) - [Server Upload Quickstart](/docs/vercel-blob/server-upload) - [Vercel Blob JS SDK Reference](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk) - [Vercel Blob Python SDK Reference](/docs/vercel-blob/python-sdk-reference) - [Vercel Blob CLI](/docs/cli/blob) - [Vercel Blob Pricing](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing) - [Vercel Blob Security](/docs/vercel-blob/security) - [Vercel Blob Examples](/docs/vercel-blob/examples) - [Observability](/docs/observability) --- [View full sitemap](/docs/sitemap) If you find anything wrong or missing or can't find something, submit feedback by reading https://vercel.com/feedback.md to improve Vercel.

Learn how Astr Full cross-link map for this page: [/docs/vercel-blob.graph.md](/docs/vercel-blob.graph.md) ## Use cases You can upload files to Vercel Blob at build time or at runtime (for example, when users submit files). Common use cases include: - Files for display and download such as avatars, screenshots, cover images, and videos - Large files such as video and audio to take advantage of the global network - Persistent preferences and context for [eve agents](#store-eve-agent-memory) - Files that you would normally store in an external file storage solution like Amazon S3. With your project hosted on Vercel, you can readily access and manage these files with Vercel Blob > **💡 Note:** Stored files are referred to as "blobs" once they're in the storage system, > following cloud storage terminology. ## Private and public storage Files are private or public depending on the store you create. The access mode defines how files are accessed and delivered. Use the following table to understand the differences between the two modes: | | Private storage | Public storage | | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | | Write access | Authenticated | Authenticated | | Read access | Authenticated (token required) | Anyone with the URL | | Delivery | Through your [Functions](/docs/functions), which fetch the blob with the SDK | Direct blob URL | | Best for | Sensitive documents, user content, custom auth | Large media, images, videos, public assets | > **💡 Note:** It's important to choose the correct access mode for your use case since you cannot change it after the creation of a blob store. Learn more about [private storage](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage) and [public storage](/docs/vercel-blob/public-storage). ## Getting started Upload a file with the Vercel Blob SDK: **index.ts** ```ts filename="index.ts" import { put } from '@vercel/blob'; const blob = await put('avatar.jpg', imageFile, { access: 'private' /* or 'public' */, }); ``` **main.py** ```py filename="main.py" from vercel import blob uploaded = await blob.put_blob( "avatar.jpg", image_bytes, access="private", # or "public" ) ``` You can create and manage your Vercel Blob stores from your [account dashboard](/dashboard) or the [Vercel CLI](/docs/cli/blob). You can create blob stores in any of the 19 [regions](/docs/regions#region-list) to optimize performance and meet data residency requirements. You can scope your Vercel Blob stores to your Hobby team or [team](/docs/accounts#creating-a-team), and [connect them to as many projects as you want](#connecting-a-store-to-your-projects). To get started, see the [server-side](/docs/vercel-blob/server-upload), or [client-side](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload) quickstart guides. Or visit the full API reference for the [JS SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk) or the [Python SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/python-sdk-reference). ## Store eve agent memory Use [eve](/docs/eve)'s built-in `fileMemory()` provider to persist short user preferences and stable facts across conversations in a [private Vercel Blob store](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage). Each memory scope has its own document, which eve recalls before each turn. The model updates memory with `save_memory` and `remove_memory` tools. To add file memory to an existing eve project, run: ```bash filename="terminal" eve add memory/file ``` Choose **Install and set up** to create the memory definition in `agent/memory/file.ts` and create or reuse a private Blob store connected to your linked project through OIDC. When you run `eve dev` locally, memory stays in the development process and clears when you restart it. For a working example, deploy the [eve Memory Agent template](/templates/eve/eve-memory-agent). The Slack assistant keeps personal preferences separate from shared channel conventions, using authenticated user and channel identities to determine who shares each memory. See the [template repository](https://github.com/vercel-labs/eve-memory-agent-template) for setup and customization. Read [Choose an eve memory provider](/kb/guide/choose-an-eve-memory-provider) for file memory configuration and a comparison with providers that support semantic retrieval or automatic capture. ## Connecting a store to your projects To read and write blobs from your code, connect the store to your project: 1. Go to your Blob store's **Projects** tab 2. Select **Connect to Project** 3. Choose the project and the environments to connect One store can serve multiple projects, and one project can use multiple stores. ### OIDC access by default Connected projects authenticate with OpenID Connect (OIDC) by default. When you connect a store, Vercel adds these environment variables to your project: | Environment variable | What it is | | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `BLOB_STORE_ID` | The id of your Blob store. The SDK pairs it with the OIDC token to authenticate requests. It's an identifier, not a secret. | | `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` | A short-lived OIDC token that Vercel issues and rotates automatically. You never handle it directly. | | `BLOB_WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_KEY` | The public key the SDK uses to verify webhook callbacks signed by Vercel Blob. It's a public value, not a secret. | The SDK reads these variables automatically, and you never need to read or pass the OIDC token yourself. Code running in [Vercel Functions](/docs/functions) and builds works out of the box. Local development works after you run `vercel env pull` once: when the token expires, the SDK refreshes it automatically using your Vercel CLI credentials. Because OIDC tokens rotate automatically, no long-lived secret can leak from your codebase or environment. Learn more about [how OIDC token federation works](/docs/oidc#how-oidc-token-federation-works). ### When to use a read-write token `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` is a long-lived static token added to your project when you create a store. OIDC takes precedence when its environment variables are present. Use the read-write token only when: - Your code runs outside Vercel, such as in a CI job or on another host - You generate client tokens for [browser uploads](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload) See Authentication in the [JS SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk#authentication) or [Python SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/python-sdk-reference#authentication) reference for the full credential resolution order. ## Using Vercel Blob in your workflow If you'd like to know whether or not Vercel Blob can be integrated into your workflow, it's worth knowing the following: - You can have one or more Vercel Blob stores per Vercel account - You can use multiple Vercel Blob stores in one Vercel project - Each Vercel Blob store can be accessed by multiple Vercel projects - Read access: - With private Blob stores: all read access requires authentication - With public Blob stores: blob URLs are accessible to anyone with the link - Write access: all writes require authentication, through [OIDC](#oidc-access-by-default) by default on Vercel, or a [read-write token](#when-to-use-a-read-write-token) elsewhere ### Transferring to another project If you need to transfer your blob store from one project to another project in the same or different team, review [Transferring your store](/docs/storage#transferring-your-store). ## Caching Vercel's [CDN cache](/docs/caching/cdn-cache) caches all blobs (private and public) for up to 1 month by default. You can customize this duration by setting a cache max age when you upload a blob. The difference is in how the cache is reached: - **Public blobs**: The browser hits the CDN cache directly. Both the CDN and browser cache the blob. See [public storage caching](/docs/vercel-blob/public-storage#caching) for full details. - **Private blobs**: Your [Function](/docs/functions) fetches the blob through the CDN, then streams the response to the browser. You separately control browser caching through the `Cache-Control` header on your Function's response. See [private storage caching](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage#caching) for recommendations. ### Important considerations when updating blobs When you delete or update (overwrite) a blob, the changes may take up to 60 seconds to propagate through our cache. However, browser caching presents additional challenges: - While our cache can update to serve the latest content, browsers will continue serving the cached version - To force browsers to fetch the updated content, add a unique query parameter to the blob URL: ```html ``` For private blobs served through your [Functions](/docs/functions), your server code can skip the propagation delay entirely and read the latest version with a [consistent read](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage#consistent-reads). For more information about updating existing blobs, see the [overwriting blobs](#overwriting-blobs) section. ### Best practice: Treat blobs as immutable For optimal performance and to avoid caching issues, consider treating blobs as immutable objects: - Instead of updating existing blobs, create new ones with different pathnames, or add a [random suffix](#alternatives-to-overwriting) when you upload - This approach avoids unexpected behaviors like outdated content appearing in your application There are still valid use cases for mutable blobs with shorter cache durations, such as a single JSON file that's updated every 5 minutes with a top list of sales or other regularly refreshed data. For these scenarios, set an appropriate cache max age when you upload and be mindful of caching behaviors. ## Overwriting blobs By default, Vercel Blob prevents you from accidentally overwriting existing blobs by using the same pathname twice. When you attempt to upload a blob with a pathname that already exists, the upload fails with an error. ### Allowing overwrites To explicitly allow overwriting an existing blob, enable overwriting when you upload: **index.ts** ```ts filename="index.ts" const blob = await put('user-profile.jpg', imageFile, { access: 'private' /* or 'public' */, allowOverwrite: true, // Enable overwriting an existing blob with the same pathname }); ``` **main.py** ```py filename="main.py" uploaded = await blob.put_blob( "user-profile.jpg", image_bytes, access="private", # or "public" allow_overwrite=True, # Enable overwriting an existing blob with the same pathname ) ``` You can allow overwrites for server uploads, and for [client uploads](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload) when your server generates the client token. ### When to use overwriting Overwriting blobs can be appropriate for certain use cases: 1. **Regularly updated files**: For files that need to maintain the same URL but contain updated content (like JSON data files or configuration files) 2. **Content with predictable update patterns**: For data that changes on a schedule and where consumers expect updates at the same URL When overwriting blobs, be aware that due to [caching](#caching), changes won't be immediately visible. Changes may take up to 60 seconds to propagate, and browser caches may need to be explicitly refreshed. For private blobs, you can read the latest version immediately with a [consistent read](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage#consistent-reads). ### Alternatives to overwriting If you want to avoid overwriting existing content (recommended for most use cases), you have two options: 1. **Add a random suffix**: The SDK adds a unique random suffix to your pathname: **index.ts** ```ts filename="index.ts" const blob = await put('avatar.jpg', imageFile, { access: 'private' /* or 'public' */, addRandomSuffix: true, // Creates a pathname like 'REDACTED.jpg' }); ``` **main.py** ```py filename="main.py" uploaded = await blob.put_blob( "avatar.jpg", image_bytes, access="private", # or "public" add_random_suffix=True, # Creates a pathname like 'REDACTED.jpg' ) ``` 2. **Generate unique pathnames programmatically**: Create unique pathnames by adding timestamps, UUIDs, or other identifiers: **index.ts** ```ts filename="index.ts" const timestamp = Date.now(); const blob = await put(`user-profile-${timestamp}.jpg`, imageFile, { access: 'private' /* or 'public' */, }); ``` **main.py** ```py filename="main.py" import time timestamp = time.time_ns() // 1_000_000 uploaded = await blob.put_blob( f"user-profile-{timestamp}.jpg", image_bytes, access="private", # or "public" ) ``` ## Conditional writes Conditional writes implement optimistic concurrency control. When writing, pass a known ETag from a previous upload, download, or metadata request. The operation only succeeds if the blob hasn't changed since that ETag was issued. If another process modified the blob in between, the ETag won't match and the SDK raises a precondition failed error. This works the same way for both private and public storage, and applies to uploads, copies, and deletes. See the [JS SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk#put) and [Python SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/python-sdk-reference#copy_blob) references for the conditional operations each SDK supports: ```js import { head, put, BlobPreconditionFailedError } from '@vercel/blob'; // 1. Read the current blob and its ETag const metadata = await head('config.json'); // 2. Write with the ETag — only succeeds if the blob hasn't changed try { await put('config.json', JSON.stringify(newConfig), { access: 'private' /* or 'public' */, allowOverwrite: true, ifMatch: metadata.etag, }); } catch (error) { if (error instanceof BlobPreconditionFailedError) { // The blob was modified by another process — retry or handle the conflict } throw error; } ``` Use conditional writes when multiple processes or users may update the same blob concurrently, such as shared configuration files or collaborative documents. ## Conditional reads Conditional reads avoid re-downloading blobs that haven't changed. Pass the ETag you received from a previous response, and if the blob is unchanged, the read returns a `304 Not Modified` status without the file content. Pass the ETag with the [`ifNoneMatch`](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk#get) option. How conditional reads work depends on how blobs are delivered: - **Private blobs**: Your [Function](/docs/functions) fetches the blob with a conditional read, then forwards the `304` or `200` response to the browser. See [browser caching with conditional requests](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage#browser-caching-with-conditional-requests) for a full example. - **Public blobs**: The CDN handles conditional requests automatically. When a browser requests a public blob URL, the CDN includes an ETag in the response. On repeat requests, the browser sends `If-None-Match` and the CDN returns `304 Not Modified` when the blob hasn't changed. See [browser caching](/docs/vercel-blob/public-storage#browser-caching-with-conditional-requests) for details. ## Blob Data Transfer Understanding Blob Data Transfer helps you manage your [usage and pricing](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing). Blob Data Transfer applies to **public blob** downloads and to your [Functions](/docs/functions) fetching private blobs from the store. When delivering private blobs to end users, [Fast Data Transfer](/docs/cdn) applies on the Function response. See [delivery costs](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing#private-and-public-storage-delivery-costs). Vercel Blob delivers content through a specialized network optimized for static assets: - **Region-based distribution**: Content is served from 19 regional hubs strategically located around the world - **Optimized for non-critical assets**: Well-suited for content "below the fold" that isn't essential for initial page rendering metrics like First Contentful Paint (FCP) or Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) - **Cost-optimized for large assets**: 3x more cost-efficient than [Fast Data Transfer](/docs/cdn) on average - **Great for media delivery**: Ideal for large media files like images, videos, and documents While [Fast Data Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-data-transfer) provides city-level, ultra-low latency, Blob Data Transfer prioritizes cost-efficiency for larger assets where ultra-low latency isn't essential. Blob Data Transfer fees apply only to downloads (outbound traffic), not uploads. See download charges for [private storage](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage#download-charges) and [public storage](/docs/vercel-blob/public-storage#download-charges), or the [pricing documentation](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing) for full details. ## Upload charges Client uploads have no data transfer charges. Server uploads incur [Fast Data Transfer](/docs/manage-cdn-usage#fast-data-transfer) charges when your Vercel application receives the file. See download and upload charge details on the [private storage](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage#upload-charges) and [public storage](/docs/vercel-blob/public-storage#upload-charges) pages. ## Choosing your Blob store region You can create Blob stores in any of the 19 [regions](/docs/regions#region-list). Use the region selector in the dashboard at blob store creation time, or use the [CLI](/docs/cli/blob) with the `--region` option. Select a region close to your customers and functions to minimize upload time. Region selection also helps meet data regulatory requirements. Vercel Blob [pricing](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing) is regionalized, so check the pricing for your selected region. You cannot change the region once the store is created. ## Simple operations Simple operations in Vercel Blob are specific read actions counted for billing purposes: - When you retrieve blob metadata without downloading the blob - When a blob is accessed by its URL and it's a cache MISS A cache MISS occurs when the blob is accessed for the first time or when its previously cached version has expired. Note that blob URL access resulting in a cache HIT does not count as a Simple Operation. ## Advanced operations Advanced operations in Vercel Blob are write, copy, and listing actions counted for billing purposes: - When you upload a blob from your server - When you upload a blob from the browser with a [client upload](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload) - When you copy an existing blob - When you list blobs in your store ### Dashboard usage counts as operations Using the Vercel Blob file browser in your dashboard will count as operations. Each time you refresh the blob list, upload files through the dashboard, or view blob details, these actions use the same API methods that count toward your usage limits and billing. Common dashboard actions that count as operations: - **Refreshing the file browser**: Lists your blobs - **Uploading files via dashboard**: Uploads each file - **Viewing blob details**: May trigger additional API calls - **Navigating folders**: Lists blobs with different prefixes If you notice unexpected increases in your operations count, check whether team members are browsing your blob store through the Vercel dashboard. For [multipart uploads](#multipart-uploads), multiple advanced operations are counted: - One operation when starting the upload - One operation for each part uploaded - One operation for completing the upload Delete operations are free of charge. They are considered advanced operations for [operation rate limits](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing#operation-rate-limits) but not for billing. ## Storage calculation Vercel Blob measures your storage usage by taking snapshots of your blob store size every 15 minutes and averages these measurements over the entire month to calculate your GB-month usage. This approach accounts for fluctuations in storage as blobs are added and removed, ensuring you're only billed for your actual usage over time, not peak usage. The Vercel dashboard displays two metrics: - **Latest value**: The most recent measurement of your blob store size - **Monthly average**: The average of all measurements throughout the billing period (this is what you're billed for) **Example:** 1. Day 1: Upload a 2GB file → Store size: 2GB 2. Day 15: Add 1GB file → Store size: 3GB 3. Day 25: Delete 2GB file → Store size: 1GB Month end billing: - Latest value: 1GB - Monthly average: ~2GB (billed amount) If no changes occur in the following month (no new uploads or deletions), each 15-minute measurement would consistently show 1 GB. In this case, your next month's billing would be exactly 1 GB/month, as your monthly average would equal your latest value. ## Multipart uploads Vercel Blob supports multipart uploads for large files, which provides significant advantages when transferring substantial amounts of data. Multipart uploads work by splitting large files into smaller chunks (parts) that are uploaded independently and then reassembled on the server. This approach offers several key benefits: - **Improved upload reliability**: If a network issue occurs during upload, only the affected part needs to be retried instead of restarting the entire upload - **Better performance**: Multiple parts can be uploaded in parallel, significantly increasing transfer speed - **Progress tracking**: More granular upload progress reporting as each part completes We recommend using multipart uploads for files larger than 100 MB. See multipart uploads in the [JS SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk#multipart-uploads) and [Python SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/python-sdk-reference#upload-a-blob-in-parts) references for how each SDK splits and uploads parts. For billing purposes, multipart uploads count as multiple advanced operations: - One operation when starting the upload - One operation for each part uploaded - One operation for completing the upload This approach ensures reliable handling of large files while maintaining the performance and efficiency expected from modern cloud storage solutions. ## Durability and availability Vercel Blob leverages [Amazon S3](https://aws.amazon.com/s3/) as its underlying storage infrastructure, providing industry-leading durability and availability: - **Durability**: Vercel Blob offers 99.999999999% (11 nines) durability. This means that even with one billion objects, you could expect to go a hundred years without losing a single one. - **Availability**: Vercel Blob provides 99.99% (4 nines) availability in a given year, ensuring that your data is accessible when you need it. These guarantees are backed by [S3's robust architecture](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/DataDurability.html), which includes automatic replication and error correction mechanisms. ## Folders and slashes Vercel Blob has folders support to organize your blobs: **index.ts** ```ts filename="index.ts" const blob = await put('folder/file.txt', 'Hello World!', { access: 'private' /* or 'public' */, }); ``` **main.py** ```py filename="main.py" uploaded = await blob.put_blob( "folder/file.txt", b"Hello World!", access="private", # or "public" ) ``` The path `folder/file.txt` creates a folder named `folder` and a blob named `file.txt`. To list all blobs within a folder, list blobs with the folder as a prefix: **index.ts** ```ts filename="index.ts" const listOfBlobs = await list({ cursor, limit: 1000, prefix: 'folder/', }); ``` **main.py** ```py filename="main.py" async for item in blob.query_blobs(prefix="folder/"): print(item.pathname) ``` To browse one folder level at a time, list only the blobs directly inside the folder along with the names of its subfolders. See browsing folders in the [JS SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk#folders) and [Python SDK](/docs/vercel-blob/python-sdk-reference#query_blob_entries) references. You don't need to create folders. Upload a file with a path containing a slash `/`, and Vercel Blob will interpret the slashes as folder delimiters. In the Vercel Blob file browser on the Vercel dashboard, any pathname with a slash `/` is treated as a folder. However, these are not actual folders like in a traditional file system; they are used for organizing blobs in listings and the file browser. ## Pathname characters Control characters in a pathname are not supported. If you upload a blob with one, the pathname and URLs returned when you list blobs may not match the blob you stored, and operations that take them may not find it. ## Blob sorting and organization When you list blobs, they're returned in **lexicographical order** by pathname (not creation date). Numbers are treated as characters, so `file10.txt` comes before `file2.txt`. **Sort by creation date:** Include timestamps in pathnames: **index.ts** ```ts filename="index.ts" const timestamp = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]; // YYYY-MM-DD await put(`reports/${timestamp}-quarterly-report.pdf`, file, { access: 'private' /* or 'public' */, }); ``` **main.py** ```py filename="main.py" from datetime import date timestamp = date.today().isoformat() # YYYY-MM-DD await blob.put_blob( f"reports/{timestamp}-quarterly-report.pdf", file_bytes, access="private", # or "public" ) ``` **Use prefixes for search:** Consider lowercase pathnames for consistent matching: **index.ts** ```ts filename="index.ts" await put('user-uploads/avatar.jpg', file, { access: 'private' /* or 'public' */, }); const userUploads = await list({ prefix: 'user-uploads/' }); ``` **main.py** ```py filename="main.py" await blob.put_blob( "user-uploads/avatar.jpg", file_bytes, access="private", # or "public" ) user_uploads = [item async for item in blob.query_blobs(prefix="user-uploads/")] ``` For complex sorting, sort results client-side using the upload time or other properties. ## More resources - [Private Storage](/docs/vercel-blob/private-storage) - [Public Storage](/docs/vercel-blob/public-storage) - [Client Upload Quickstart](/docs/vercel-blob/client-upload) - [Server Upload Quickstart](/docs/vercel-blob/server-upload) - [Vercel Blob JS SDK Reference](/docs/vercel-blob/using-blob-sdk) - [Vercel Blob Python SDK Reference](/docs/vercel-blob/python-sdk-reference) - [Vercel Blob CLI](/docs/cli/blob) - [Vercel Blob Pricing](/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing) - [Vercel Blob Security](/docs/vercel-blob/security) - [Vercel Blob Examples](/docs/vercel-blob/examples) - [Observability](/docs/observability) --- [View full sitemap](/docs/sitemap) If you find anything wrong or missing or can't find something, submit feedback by reading https://vercel.com/feedback.md to improve Vercel.

I'd split the decision in two: **where the files live** and **what people look at**. Everything below assumes the kits and runs stay out of the `discourse-graph` repo, as you want.

## Two facts that shape the options
- **Playwright's trace viewer is a 1.6 MB static bundle** shipped inside `playwright-core`. We can host it next to the traces on the same domain. Then "Open trace" is a plain link: no CORS, no `npx`, nothing to install.
- **Vercel Blob has both public and private stores.** Our existing store, the one behind `discoursegraphs.com/releases/*` that the Roam PR builds publish to, is **public**. A private store needs a small server function to read from it, or signed URLs.

## Where the files live

| | Kits (small JSON, the test cases) | Runs (results, ~10–80 MB traces, screenshots) |
|---|---|---|
| **Vercel Blob only** | Versioned paths (`kits/eng-2228/v3.json`) + a manifest. No diff or review of kit changes | ✅ natural fit |
| **Separate git repo** (e.g. `DiscourseGraphs/proof-kits`) | ✅ history, diffs, PR review when a case changes, which is your "update the test for regressions" | ❌ too big for git; put them in Blob |

**Recommendation:** start with Blob for everything, since that's the least setup. Move kits into a small separate repo once people start editing cases and want them reviewed. Traces stay in Blob either way.

## What people look at

| Option | What it is | Pros | Cons | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Static catalog on Blob** (recommended for the MVP) | One `index.html` + `manifest.json` + the self-hosted trace viewer, under `/releases/proof/` | No server to run; one link for everyone; "Open trace" opens the viewer at that run; publishing is one CLI command after a run | Public if it uses the existing store, so test-vault/graph content only (it is test data already); no logins, so no approve/decline buttons | **S** |
| **B. A page in `apps/website`** (`/proof`) reading a **private** Blob store | Next.js page + a function that streams blobs | Private, behind existing auth; room to grow into approve/decline and comparing a PR's run against `main` | UI code lives in the codebase (the kits still don't); needs auth and a function | **M** |
| **C. Claude Artifact** | Org-private page with stored data | Approve/decline buttons and comments come for free; nothing to host | Traces are too big (20 MB cap, `.zip` not accepted), so it would only link to Blob; tied to claude.ai | **S** |
| **D. Storybook** | Its catalog UI, with each case as a "story" | The organisation you liked | Stories render components in its own iframe; it can't run Roam or Obsidian. We'd only borrow the shell, at the cost of keeping a Storybook build alive | **M**, low value |
| **E. Playwright HTML report** | Playwright's built-in list of tests + status + trace | Exactly "all tests, green/red, click into the trace" | We'd have to fake its internal report format, which isn't a public API, so it would break on upgrades | **M**, brittle |
| **F. Hosted dashboards** (Currents, Argos, Allure TestOps) | Test-reporting SaaS | History, trends, flakiness | Built for Playwright test-runner output, not our kits; paid; data leaves us | **M**, $$ |

**Recommendation:** start with **A** for the MVP. Keep Storybook's *organisation* (a sidebar tree, a status badge per case, a detail panel) without Storybook itself. Move to **B** when it needs to be private or interactive. Option C stays useful only for the approve/decline step.

## The MVP as a sketch

```
discoursegraphs.com/releases/proof/                     last published 2026-10-26 16:10
┌──────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ▾ Obsidian                   │ Case 2/8 · Add a page link to a text shape     ✅ pass │
│   ▾ Canvas · links           │ Kit eng-2228 · proves Done When 2                     │
│     ✅ Text shape offers Edit │ Passes if: the text shape stores the link, and the    │
│     ✅ Add a page link   ◀    │   link button shows beside it                         │
│     ✅ Open the link          │                                                       │
│     ✅ Persists on reopen     │ Last runs                                             │
│     ✅ Edit / ✅ Remove        │   ✅ 2026-10-26  build c0d00c2  8/8   [Open trace]    │
│     ✅ Geo https  ✅ Geo page  │   ✅ 2026-10-15  build c0d00c2  8/8   [Open trace]    │
│     ⊘ Rejected: action URIs  │                                                       │
│   ▸ Node format (eng-2176)   │ Steps: 1 close menus · 2 … · 9 save the link          │
│ ▸ Roam                       │ Rejected cases stay listed, with their reasons        │
└──────────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**How it would work:**
- **Organised by app, then feature, then case**, not by ticket. That way it grows into a regression catalogue: each case shows its latest run, and a PR's run sits next to the last run on `main`.
- **Publishing:** after a run, `proof publish` uploads it to `proof/runs/<app>/<kit>/<run>/` (results, records, `trace.zip`) and updates `proof/manifest.json`. The page is a single static file that reads the manifest.
- **Trace size:** a published trace can drop the filmstrip and keep the Before/After snapshots. That's roughly 10× smaller than the 76 MB we got. Storage cost is negligible either way.

## Decisions I need from you
1. **Public is fine for the MVP?** Traces contain only test-vault and test-graph content, but anyone with the link could open them. Or go private from day one (option B, more work)?
2. **Kits in Blob only, or in a small separate repo** for history and review?
3. **Who publishes:** local runs only for now, or CI later? CI would need a signed-in Roam account and an Obsidian install, which is a separate project.

If you pick A, I'll build `proof publish` and the catalog page. I'll check them locally first, then upload to Blob, but only once you say so, since uploading publishes them.

--- title: Vercel Blob Pricing product: vercel url: /docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing canonical_url: "https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-blob/usage-and-pricing" last_updated: 2026-09-23 type: reference prerequisites: - /docs/vercel-blob related: - /docs/manage-cdn-usage - /docs/cdn - /docs/vercel-blob/client-upload - /docs/vercel-blob/server-upload - /docs/vercel-blob summary: Learn about the pricing for Vercel Blob. install_vercel_plugin: npx plugins add vercel/vercel-plugin --- # Vercel Blob Pricing > Vercel Blob is available on all plans > > Those with the owner, member, developer role can access this feature ## Usage Vercel Blob usage is measured based on the following: ## Related pages > **For AI agents:** Follow these links to understand how this page connects to the rest of the Vercel ecosystem. For the full cross-link map (inbound, outbound, prerequisites, and semantic neighbors), see the .graph.md link below. - [The Complete Guide to Vercel Blob](https://vercel.com/kb/guide/vercel-blob) — Vercel Blob stores and serves files of any size through Vercel's global network.
